action_summary: The transfer store keyed every closed goal on the constant string "goal", so recall matched across goals and wrote false successes to disk. The key is now the effect the goal asks for, both parts already computed by the route before the key is used: "effect|target=<target>|suffix=<suffix>". The goal's words are deliberately NOT part of the key, because two sentences asking for the same file in the same format are the same job, and keying on prose would rebuild the paraphrase cache-miss cost that fingerprint_key was rewritten to remove (its own comment measures that at ~1268 ms per new name against ~265 ms for a repeat). The change is one line plus the measurement that justifies it.
blocker_lease_key: 2026-10-09-resource-bounded-bytes-v1::GENERAL_REUSABLE_PROBLEM_SOLVING_CAPABILITY_FRONTIER::A learned success was not a memory of the goal it succeeded at. computer_env_v1._discover_impl kept every closed goal under the constant gkey="goal", while the fingerprint deliberately excludes the target, so the goal's identity appeared nowhere in the memory key and recall matched across goals. Measured 2026-11-16 on this machine: thirteen unrelated goals left thirteen rows in the transfer store, every one recording reached=True, with plans naming whatever single program happened to touch the target first -- run_iconv for one goal, run_gp-display-src for another, x86_64-linux-gnu-cpp for another, run_unexpand for another, run_bzip2 for one that really did compress. A row for a wrong program was indistinguishable from a row for a right one. Answers were saved only because _verify_plan re-executes a recalled plan against the target actually requested; every other reader of the store -- audits, similarity scoring, episode counts, and the evidence bonus in transfer_learning_v1.recall -- was reading a plan labelled correct that was not.
